questions.question: When can we say that the whole of an object is floating on water?
options: Only if it is completely above the surface of the water.
If any part of the object remains above the water's surface.
Only if exactly half of its volume is below the surface.
If it is fully submerged but not touching the bottom.

questions.question: A student wants to test if a toy boat floats better in a deep swimming pool or a shallow tray of water. What will they find?
options: It floats better in the pool because deep water has more upthrust.
It floats better in the tray because shallow water is more dense.
How well it floats does not depend on the depth of the liquid.
It will only float in the deep pool and will sink in the shallow tray.

questions.question: Under what condition will an object float in water?
options: If its shape can push its own mass of water out of the way without going under.
If its total mass is exactly 1 kilogram regardless of shape.
If it is made entirely of hollow metal tubes.
If its shape prevents any water from being displaced.

questions.question: Approximately how much force is needed to lift a 1 kg mass on Earth?
options: 1 N

questions.question: How many grams are there in 1 kilogram?
What is the correct formula used to calculate gravitational force (Weight)?
options: W = m × g
W = m ÷ g
W = g ÷ m
W = m + g

questions.question: If you add equal-sized increases in force to a spring, how does its extension change?
options: The extension increases by the same amount each time.
The extension doubles with every single increase.
The extension increases by smaller and smaller amounts.
The extension stops increasing after the first force is added.

questions.question: Why is a metal spring described as being elastic?
options: Because it can be melted down and remoulded easily.
Because it returns to its original length when a force is removed.
Because it breaks immediately when a small force is applied.
Because its extension is always twice the force applied to it.

questions.question: Which scientific law specifically describes the behaviour of springs when stretched?
options: Newton's Third Law
Hooke's Law
Pascal's Law
Archimedes' Principle

questions.question: What can a lever do to help us lift heavy objects?
options: It can multiply a small force into a larger force.
It can decrease the total weight of the object being lifted.
It can completely eliminate the force of gravity.
It can increase the mass of the person using it.

questions.question: What distinguishes the different types (classes) of levers from each other?
options: The material the lever is made from.
The position of the pivot.
The total mass of the lever itself.
The speed at which the lever is moved.

questions.question: What does pressure measure?
options: How concentrated a force is over an area.
The total mass of an object.
The speed at which an object moves.
The total energy stored in a spring.

questions.question: What is the formula used to calculate pressure?
options: Pressure = force × area
Pressure = force ÷ area
Pressure = area ÷ force
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit "newtons per square metre" (N/m²)?
options: Joule (J)
Pascal (Pa)
Newton (N)
Watt (W)

questions.question: How does the surface area of a boat's hull affect the upthrust on it?
options: A larger surface area allows a bigger upthrust on the hull.
A larger surface area reduces the maximum possible upthrust.
Surface area has no effect on the upthrust.
A smaller surface area always increases the upthrust.

questions.question: Why does the pressure in a liquid increase as you go deeper?
options: Because the liquid becomes significantly hotter at the bottom.
Because there is more liquid above pushing down.
Because the particles in the liquid expand at depth.
Because the liquid is moving faster at the bottom.

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure reduce with height?
options: Because there is less air above pushing down.
Because gravity becomes zero at high altitudes.
Because the temperature of the air always increases.
Because the air molecules become much heavier.

questions.question: How does a rubber band behave compared to a spring when equal-sized increases in force are applied?
options: Its extension increases by the same amount for each force increase.
Its extension increases by different amounts for each equal-sized increase in force.
It does not extend at all until a threshold force is met.
Its extension is always directly proportional to the force applied.

questions.question: What is the physical effect caused by a moment?
options: It causes an object to speed up in a straight line.
It causes turning.
It changes the mass of an object.
It increases the density of a liquid.

questions.question: How do you calculate the moment of a force?
options: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force ÷ perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force + perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = perpendicular distance ÷ force
